newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Channel 5 signs movie deal with Fox.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Channel 5 signs movie deal with Fox.

text.p: Britain's new Channel 5, which is due to launch next March, on Wednesday signed a movie deal with 20th Century Fox International that will allow it to show terrestrial television premieres of hit films including Independence Day.
The deal, which includes 68 first-run films, was negotiated jointly with the BBC but only nine of the 68 premieres will be shared.
The new station plans to show the 37 films it has taken exclusively in the peak weekday slot.
Channel 5 is owned by a consortium comprising Pearson, United News, Luxembourg broadcast group CLT and Warburg Pincus of the U.S. whle Fox is part of Rupert Murdoch's News Corp.
Channel 5's Director of Programmes Dawn Airey said, "This is a key deal for 5. We are serious about film and we will be showing top movies every night of the week."
Other titles exclusive to Channel 5 include Braveheart, Courage Under Fire, Speed and Mrs Doubtfire.
Channel 5 declined to comment on how much the deal cost.
